meta.title: Fate Tutor — Destiny Intelligence, the Ancient Wisdom Engine
meta.description: Read your birth through several ancient traditions, each kept separate and each showing its source. Worked out on your own device.
hero.title: The Ancient Wisdom Engine
hero.lead: Understand destiny. Explore possibilities. Develop your life.
hero.body: Enter your birth details once. Each ancient tradition then reads them in its own way, on its own terms. Nothing is blended, and every statement shows where it comes from.
hero.promise1.title: Never mixed
hero.promise1.body: Each tradition has its own calculator and its own rulebook. They are shown side by side, never merged into one score.
hero.promise2.title: Calculated, not made up
hero.promise2.body: Charts come from calculators checked against NASA's figures and established calendars.
hero.promise3.title: Honest about what it is
hero.promise3.body: These are traditions, not science, and not predictions. They describe tendencies, never certainties.
found.title: One foundation, six branches
found.body: Destiny Intelligence is where Fate Tutor begins. What it finds becomes the starting point for the rest of your life journey.

result.separate: Each tradition below is worked out and read on its own. A side-by-side comparison comes in a later stage.

bazi.title: BaZi 八字 — the Four Pillars
bazi.intro: Four pairs of characters, one each for the year, month, day and hour of birth. The upper character of the day pillar is your Day Master: the character that stands for you.
bazi.elements: The five elements in your chart
bazi.elements.body: A simple count of the visible characters. It is a fact about the chart, not a judgement of strength.
bazi.year_rule: The BaZi year turns at Start of Spring (立春), around 4 February. Your BaZi year is {year}.
bazi.month_rule: Your BaZi month opened at {opens} ({opens_time}) and closes at {closes} ({closes_time}), Beijing time.
bazi.tengods.title: The Ten Gods among your visible stems
bazi.tengods.body: A Ten God names how another character relates to your Day Master.
bazi.luck.title: Ten-year luck cycles (大运)
bazi.luck.forward: Your cycles run forward through the sixty pairs.
bazi.luck.backward: Your cycles run backward through the sixty pairs.
bazi.luck.start: The first cycle begins at about age {age}. Tradition counts three days to the neighbouring solar term ({term}) as one year.
bazi.luck.approx: Without a birth time the starting age is approximate.
bazi.luck.none: Luck cycles need the sex to be given, because their direction depends on it.
bazi.flow: This year ({year}) is a {name} year. To your Day Master its stem is the {god}.
zodiac.title: Chinese zodiac 生肖
zodiac.intro: Twelve animals in a twelve-year round, each year also carrying one of the five elements.
zodiac.by_new_year: Counted from Lunar New Year (the popular way)
zodiac.by_spring: Counted from Start of Spring (the way BaZi counts)
numerology.title: Numerology
numerology.intro: The modern Pythagorean system. Numbers are added digit by digit down to a single digit, except 11, 22 and 33, which are kept as “master numbers”.
numerology.other_method: Some teachers add every digit of the date in one go. That method gives {number}.
numerology.name.not_given: Enter your full birth name to see the name numbers.
numerology.name.not_latin_letters: This system counts the 26 Latin letters only. A name in another script belongs to a different tradition, so no name numbers are shown.
weton.title: Javanese Weton
weton.intro: The seven-day week and the five-day market week (pasaran) meet on your birthday. The pair returns every 35 days.
weton.sunset: You were born in the evening. In Javanese reckoning the day begins at sunset, which would make your weton {name} (neptu {neptu}). Both are shown; ask your family which was used.
rule.bazi.day_master.jia: Tradition pictures Jia Wood (甲) as a tall tree: upright, strong and growing steadily upward. It is said to flourish with warmth.
rule.bazi.day_master.yi: Tradition pictures Yi Wood (乙) as leaves, flowers and climbing plants: soft and flexible, yet able to work its way through hard ground, and at its best with something to lean on.
rule.bazi.day_master.bing: Tradition pictures Bing Fire (丙) as the blazing sun: fierce, generous and open, unafraid of frost and snow.
rule.bazi.day_master.ding: Tradition pictures Ding Fire (丁) as a lamp flame: gentle on the outside, bright and clear within, burning steadily rather than fiercely.
rule.bazi.day_master.wu: Tradition pictures Wu Earth (戊) as a mountain: solid, weighty, centred and upright, the ground that other things rely on.
rule.bazi.day_master.ji: Tradition pictures Ji Earth (己) as garden soil: humble and moist, centred, quietly storing and nurturing what grows in it.
rule.bazi.day_master.geng: Tradition pictures Geng Metal (庚) as raw iron: tough, direct and strong-willed. It is said to be cleared by Water and sharpened by Fire.
rule.bazi.day_master.xin: Tradition describes Xin Metal (辛) as gentle, warm and clear: a refined and sensitive kind of strength.
rule.bazi.day_master.ren: Tradition pictures Ren Water (壬) as a great river: always moving, firm at its core, flowing around obstacles without standing still.
rule.bazi.day_master.gui: Tradition pictures Gui Water (癸) as rain and dew: the softest water, yet it reaches everywhere and quietly nourishes.
rule.bazi.ten_god.bi_jian: The Friend (比肩) is the same element as you. Tradition reads it as self-reliance, and as peers who stand alongside you.
rule.bazi.ten_god.jie_cai: Rob Wealth (劫财) is a peer star: companions and rivals. The old text speaks of competition among equals over shared resources.
rule.bazi.ten_god.shi_shen: The Eating God (食神) stands for ease, enjoyment and natural expression. The old text links it with a generous, contented nature.
rule.bazi.ten_god.shang_guan: The Hurting Officer (伤官) stands for talent, outspokenness and independence. The old text describes many skills together with a proud streak that questions authority.
rule.bazi.ten_god.pian_cai: Indirect Wealth (偏财) is the second wealth star: resources that come through opportunity and dealings with many people. Tradition adds that one needs the capacity to manage them.
rule.bazi.ten_god.zheng_cai: Direct Wealth (正财) stands for steady, earned resources. The old text stresses having the strength to make use of them: enough at the right time matters more than a great amount.
rule.bazi.ten_god.qi_sha: Seven Killings (七杀) is the traditional name for a demanding, competitive force: pressure, challenge and drive. The old text says it serves well when it is kept under discipline.
rule.bazi.ten_god.zheng_guan: The Direct Officer (正官) stands for rules, duty and recognised standing. The old text calls it a noble star that does best when left undisturbed.
rule.bazi.ten_god.pian_yin: The Indirect Resource (偏印) stands for unconventional learning and an independent mind. The old text cautions that things may be started and left unfinished.
rule.bazi.ten_god.zheng_yin: The Direct Resource (正印) stands for support, learning and protection. The old text links it with thoughtfulness and with help received from elders.
rule.zodiac.animal.rat: Popular tradition associates the Rat with being quick-witted, resourceful and alert.
rule.zodiac.animal.ox: Popular tradition associates the Ox with being steady, patient and hard-working.
rule.zodiac.animal.tiger: Popular tradition associates the Tiger with being bold, competitive and warm-hearted.
rule.zodiac.animal.rabbit: Popular tradition associates the Rabbit with being gentle, careful and tactful.
rule.zodiac.animal.dragon: Popular tradition associates the Dragon with being confident, ambitious and full of energy.
rule.zodiac.animal.snake: Popular tradition associates the Snake with being thoughtful, perceptive and private.
rule.zodiac.animal.horse: Popular tradition associates the Horse with being lively, independent and always on the move.
rule.zodiac.animal.goat: Popular tradition associates the Goat with being gentle, creative and considerate.
rule.zodiac.animal.monkey: Popular tradition associates the Monkey with being clever, curious and playful.
rule.zodiac.animal.rooster: Popular tradition associates the Rooster with being observant, hard-working and outspoken.
rule.zodiac.animal.dog: Popular tradition associates the Dog with being loyal, honest and protective.
rule.zodiac.animal.pig: Popular tradition associates the Pig with being generous, easy-going and sincere.
rule.numerology.number.1: In this system the number 1 is linked with independence, initiative and making a start.
rule.numerology.number.2: In this system the number 2 is linked with cooperation, sensitivity and bringing people together.
rule.numerology.number.3: In this system the number 3 is linked with expression, creativity and sociability.
rule.numerology.number.4: In this system the number 4 is linked with order, steady work and building things that last.
rule.numerology.number.5: In this system the number 5 is linked with freedom, change and curiosity.
rule.numerology.number.6: In this system the number 6 is linked with care, responsibility and home.
rule.numerology.number.7: In this system the number 7 is linked with analysis, study and an inner search.
rule.numerology.number.8: In this system the number 8 is linked with ambition, organisation and managing resources.
rule.numerology.number.9: In this system the number 9 is linked with compassion, a broad outlook and giving back.
rule.numerology.number.11: In this system 11 is a master number, linked with intuition and inspiration. It is also read as 2.
rule.numerology.number.22: In this system 22 is a master number, linked with turning large ideas into practical form. It is also read as 4.
rule.numerology.number.33: In this system 33 is a master number, linked with teaching and caring for others. It is also read as 6.
rule.weton.neptu: The Primbon tradition gives each day and each market day a value and adds them. Yours add up to {neptu}. Tradition uses this total when comparing two birthdays and when choosing days. Fate Tutor shows the total and does not judge it.
note.time_unknown: No birth time was given. The hour pillar is left out, and anything that depends on the time of day is marked approximate.
note.no_longitude_clock_used: No birthplace position was available, so the clock time was used instead of true sun time.
note.summer_time: Clocks were on summer time at this birth, one hour ahead. True sun time already allows for that.
note.skipped_hour: Clocks were moved forward at this moment, so this clock time never existed. The reading uses the clock as it was before the change.
note.repeated_hour: Clocks were moved back at this moment, so this clock time happened twice. The first occurrence is used.
note.pre_1970_clock: For births before 1970 the clock history follows each zone's main city. A smaller town may have kept different clocks.
note.late_zi_hour: This birth falls between 23:00 and midnight. Schools differ on whether that hour belongs to the same day or the next. You can switch the rule under “Settings where schools differ”.
note.near_term: This birth is only {seconds} seconds from a solar term, where the month pillar changes. A small error in the recorded time would change the chart.
note.term_on_birth_day: A solar term falls on this birth day. Without the birth time, the month pillar could be on either side of it.
note.sex_not_given: Sex was not given, so the BaZi luck cycles are left out.
note.lunar_uncertain: This lunar date sits next to a new moon that falls within minutes of midnight, so the lunar day could be one off.
note.zodiac_conventions_differ: You were born between 1 January and the turn of the Chinese year. The two ways of counting give different animals, so both are shown.
legal.title: How we work
legal.tradition: These are traditional systems of belief. They are not science and they do not predict the future. Fate Tutor shows what each tradition says and where it says it, in the language of tendencies.
legal.offlimits: We do not give readings about death, lifespan, serious illness, accidents or disasters, even where old texts do.
legal.advice: For decisions about health, money, law or marriage, please speak to a qualified professional. A traditional reading is a perspective, not advice.
legal.review: Readings marked “awaiting expert review” follow a named source but have not yet been checked by a practitioner.
legal.privacy: Your birth details stay on your device. This page does not store or send them.
legal.hosting: This page is delivered by GitHub Pages, and its fonts by Google Fonts. As with any website, those services see your internet address when the page loads. Fate Tutor sets no cookies and does no tracking; it remembers only your language choice, on your own device.
legal.credits: City data: GeoNames (geonames.org), CC BY 4.0. Classical texts read from Chinese Wikisource. Calculators checked against NASA JPL Horizons.
